corpusSnapshot.provenance: Synthetic authored posts with two independent rubric-based label sets. Own-intent gold is authored; other-intent gold is false. Ambiguous pairs are excluded from headline scores. Diagnostic twins are separate from scored posts.

intents.rubric: Hide posts where the author is gratuitously rude toward people: insulting, demeaning or sneering at a person or group far beyond what any point needs; name-calling; telling someone to die or kill themselves; or using slurs (ethnic, racial, homophobic, transphobic, ableist, misogynist and similar), whether aimed at someone or dropped casually for shock value. Performative contempt meant to look edgy or draw attention counts, including short insult-only replies to strangers and sarcastic contempt without swear words. Keep: posts that criticise, report, complain about or quote rudeness or slurs in order to object to them; discussion of a word's meaning or history; swearing that is not aimed at anyone (for example at a printer or the weather); clearly affectionate banter between friends; slang that sounds violent but is praise or laughter ('killing it', 'I'm dead'); blunt but sincere criticism of ideas, work or public conduct, and angry complaints without insults; low-content replies (reach-boosting replies such as 'commenting for reach', 'following', '+1', a lone emoji, or only tags); and ordinary posts.

labels.W0: performative rudeness that are execessive like unnecessary usage of slurs
labels.W1: performative rudeness that are excessive like unnecessary usage of slurs
labels.W4: posts being deliberately rude or edgy to get attention
labels.W5: posts insulting people or using slurs
labels.W6: posts that insult someone or use slurs
labels.W7: insults, slurs and name-calling aimed at people
labels.W8: posts where the author insults people or uses slurs
labels.W11: posts mocking or insulting people to look edgy
labels.W12: posts insulting or attacking a person

intents.rubric: Hide posts that make sweeping claims that society, the economy, the planet or 'everything' is collapsing or already lost and that nothing can be done, whether said outright or through sarcastic resignation. Keep specific factual reporting of bad news, worried posts that point to action or solutions, critiques of doomism, and personal bad-day hyperbole about the author's own small mishaps.
intents.label: posts saying everything is collapsing and it's hopeless

intents.rubric: Hide posts that mock, ridicule or invite a pile-on against an ordinary, non-public person's post, mistake or behaviour for laughs, including screenshot dunks, sarcastic quote-posts and 'everyone look at this' callouts, whether open or veiled. Keep posts that criticise dunk culture, laugh at the poster's own mistakes, gently correct misinformation without ridicule, and criticise public institutions or officials on the substance of what they did.
intents.label: posts mocking a random person's post or mistake

intents.rubric: Hide posts built mainly to get replies rather than to share anything or ask a real question: 'wrong answers only', 'which one are you', 'drop your X below', 'name a Y that Z', this-or-that picks, and vague prompts meant only to fill the replies, whether open or dressed up as casual chat. Keep real questions where the poster actually needs information or input, posts with real content that end with a natural question, practical requests for replies that serve a concrete purpose, and posts criticising engagement bait.
intents.label: posts asking questions just to get replies

intents.rubric: Hide posts that show off an achievement, status, wealth, looks or popularity while presenting it as a complaint, a burden, gratitude, self-deprecation or modesty, so that the brag is the real point. Keep open, sincere celebrations of good news, including ones that mention past struggle, real complaints and venting, modest posts about small personal wins that are not dressed up, and posts that mock or criticise humblebragging.
intents.label: posts bragging while pretending to complain or be humble

intents.rubric: Hide posts that glorify or promote overwork as a virtue: bragging about long hours, little sleep, no days off, or pre-dawn routines framed as what separates winners from everyone else, and posts that shame rest or balance. Keep posts that criticise or mock hustle culture, sincere burnout or recovery stories, plain descriptions of an early routine or heavy workload that do not hold it up as a moral standard, and people working long hours out of necessity without glorifying it.
intents.label: posts glorifying overwork, 5am routines and grinding

intents.rubric: Hide posts where the author is deliberately rude, sneering or contemptuous toward other people as a performance: insulting strangers or repliers, dismissing people as stupid or worthless, or posing as tough or 'unbothered' to get attention or engagement. Sarcastic or understated contempt aimed at people counts. Keep posts that are blunt but sincere critique of ideas or work, plain disagreement with reasons, posts that criticise or complain about rude behaviour (including quoting it to object), and ordinary posts.
intents.label: posts being deliberately rude or edgy to get attention

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: exaggerated claims that artificial intelligence will solve everything.
intents.label: exaggerated claims that artificial intelligence will solve everything

intents.label: gossip about famous entertainers or celebrities

intents.label: cryptocurrency investing or promotion

intents.label: personal feuds or public insults between people

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: requests for likes, reposts, or replies to boost engagement.
intents.label: requests for likes, reposts, or replies to boost engagement

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: exercise routines and fitness training.
intents.label: exercise routines and fitness training

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: food and cooking.
intents.label: food and cooking

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: government policy or election politics.
intents.label: government policy or election politics

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: promotion of the author's own product or paid service.
intents.label: promotion of the author's own product or paid service

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: rage bait. For categories like "rage bait" or "outrage farming", answer yes only when the post is engineered to provoke anger or amplify a pile-on: repost/share/quote/tag requests, ratio calls, "make this loud" framing, "wake up" outrage escalation, or language that pushes readers to attack or shame a target. Answer no for sincere frustration, fair criticism, personal hardship, civic participation, ordinary sarcasm, or calm pessimism unless the post is also trying to farm outrage.
intents.label: rage bait

intents.rubric: Hide posts about or doing: sports results or commentary.
intents.label: sports results or commentary
